Scotts Cove
Darien, Conn.
Nov. 8, 1966
Dear Debby:
I have just talked to Marvin McFarland, by phone, at
the Library of Congress.
He says he remembers well discussing
with Bix the question of the gift of letters, papers, records,
etc., and that the process you are following id the correct
one•
The shipment should be addressed to Mr. Jennings Wood,
Processing Department, Exchange and Gift Division, as Jou
were planning on doing. McFarland will contact Mr. Wood to
alert him for the arrival of the shipment.
I said you would
probably send it within days or at most a
few weeks.
McFarland advises that you write a letter to Mr. Wood
at the same time the papers are shipped. He says you will
then receive an acknowledgement from the Library together
with a gift-form for your signature -- the routine procedure.
I am glad these papers are going to the Library of
Congress, and do not feel they could be sent to a better
place.
They will form a very valuable part of the records
of the period of American, and world-wide development which
Harold's life spanned and
influenced in a quiet but extra-
ordinary way.
It was really good to hear from you this morning and
to be in contact again.
I wish I were not leaving for
Europe tonight, and that we could get together here or in
New York for an evening.
Many thanks for your invitation to Captiva. It is,
as I said, years since I have been on the island. I hope
very much Anne and I can come and see you there sometime.
Best wishes always,
Chanen
